chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From what point does the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') differ from the Mu'tamir (one who performs Umrah)? He said: Indeed, the Mutamatti' is bound to the Hajj, but the Mu'tamir, once he has finished from it, goes wherever he wishes. And Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) performed Umrah in Dhi al-Hijjah, then departed on the Day of Tawriyah to Iraq, while the people were departing to Mina. Therefore, there is no harm in performing Umrah in Dhi al-Hijjah for one who does not intend Hajj.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: Mutamatti': One who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, keeping the two rituals distinct.
key_terms.الْمُعْتَمِرُ: Mu'tamir: One who performs Umrah alone, without the intention of Hajj.
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhi al-Hijjah: The twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, during which Hajj is performed.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: La ba'sa: There is no harm; permissible.
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّوْرِيَةِ: Day of Tawriyah: The 8th of Dhi al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a Mutamatti' and a Mu'tamir in Shia jurisprudence, and is Umrah permitted in Dhi al-Hijjah for those not performing Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the Mutamatti' (who remains in the state of ihram for Hajj) and the Mu'tamir (who performs Umrah alone and is free to depart). It establishes the permissibility of Umrah in Dhi al-Hijjah for those not performing Hajj by citing the precedent of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who performed Umrah and then traveled to Iraq while the pilgrims proceeded to Mina, thereby validating the 'Umrah al-Mubtulah' (Umrah performed in the months of Hajj) for individual travelers.
